Jonas / Karthik,

Thanks again for the walkthrough earlier this week. Attached is NovusCloud's redline of Exhibit B (pricing schedule) with a handful of commercial asks we need to resolve ahead of procurement sign-off. The two items blocking our GC right now are: 1) the "rebate sink" carveout in section 4.2 (Novus wants the ability to retain accumulated rebates in the event of an early exit) and 2) the "tier exit" trigger in section 6 (the language as written effectively resets discounts retroactively if we dip below the committed threshold during the term).

High-level asks:
- Can Redwood accept a clause that preserves earned rebates on termination (Novus view) OR provide a capped clawback limited to 90 days post-exit?
- Can we clarify that tier exits will be prospective only (no retroactive true-up beyond the quarter of change)?
- We also have some packaging questions on bundled SKUs that affect the stair-step discounts — see inline comments.

Our timeline: procurement needs a negotiated mark and countersign no later than EOD 2025-03-27 to meet next quarter's budgeting cycle. Can we get internal feedback and, ideally, a short call to align?

Maya — thanks for sending this over and for the clear notes. Karthik and I reviewed the redline quickly this morning. High-level reaction:

- Rebate sink: we understand the commercial ask to preserve earned rebates on termination. Legal will push back on an unlimited sink. From a pricing perspective we're open to a limited carveout (e.g., preserve credits up to 90 days after termination) or a capped percentage of the accrued rebate pool.
- Tier exit: we agree that retroactive resets beyond the quarter could be disruptive. We can propose prospective-only effect with a pro-rata true-up limited to the quarter boundary.
- Bundled SKUs: need to nail the SKU mapping rules (which items count toward the bundle threshold). We can provide a binding SKU mapping appendix if Novus can commit to a single SKU family per bundle.

I'm looping in Legal (Laura) and Deal Ops (Marissa) to draft concrete language. I've attached an internal notes workbook that outlines the concession envelope we'd need to remain margin-neutral.

Propose a quick 30-min call Monday 3/24 at 10am PT to run through the proposed compromise. If that doesn't work, offer slots for 11:30am or 2pm.

Team — quick legal take and a proposed compromise we can present to Novus. I'm pasting suggested redline snippets below so the commercial team can see the exact trade-offs.

1) Rebate accrual / sink
Proposed language (compromise):
"Notwithstanding anything to the contrary, Customer shall retain any earned rebate credits accumulated during the Term up to a maximum of ninety (90) days following termination or expiration of this Agreement. Any rebate credits in excess of the ninety (90)-day cap shall be forfeited upon termination. For the avoidance of doubt, forfeited rebate credits shall not be applied to any post-termination invoices or refunds."

Rationale: preserves some of Novus' ask while protecting Redwood from open-ended liability. If Sales wants to be more generous, we can increase the cap or convert excess to a one-time credit with a fixed dollar cap.

2) Tier exit / true-up
Proposed language (compromise):
"If Customer's usage in any given quarter falls below the commitment threshold for the applicable tier, Customer's tier and associated discounts shall be adjusted prospectively in the next billing quarter. Any true-up shall be limited to usage occurring in the quarter in which the change occurred and shall not be applied retroactively to prior invoiced periods beyond that quarter."

Rationale: removes retroactive clawbacks while allowing quarterly reconciliation.

3) Bundled SKU mapping (ops-friendly appendix)
We should include a binding SKU appendix that enumerates SKUs that count toward bundle thresholds. Language: "Customer and Vendor shall agree in writing to an SKU mapping appendix within ten (10) business days following Effective Date; absent such agreement, the parties shall default to the Vendor's SKU classification for purposes of tier calculation."

Budget impact: per Jonas' notes, if we accept the 90-day rebate sink cap with a 10% cap on excess conversion, we estimate an NPV impact of ~2.1% on the overall deal economics. Sales — please confirm whether that is within concession approval or whether we need to escalate for credit.

Attachment: legal_clause_suggestions.docx (contains full redline)

Happy to join the call Monday. Laura

Laura Bennett

Maya / Novus team — following internal review and Laura's suggested language, please find Redwood's proposed compromise below and attached as a redlined Exhibit B. Summary of the key commercial points: 

- Rebate accrual: Redwood will preserve earned rebate credits up to 90 days post-termination. Credits above the 90-day cap will be forfeited unless the parties agree to convert excess to a one-time credit not to exceed 10% of the accrued amount.
- Tier exit: tier changes will be prospective only. Any reconciliation is limited to the quarter in which the usage decrease occurred and will not be applied retroactively beyond that quarter.
- Bundled SKUs: we propose executing a binding SKU mapping appendix within 10 business days of the Effective Date. If no appendix is agreed, default to Redwood's SKU classifications for tier calculations.

Attachments: redwood_proposed_exhibitB_redline.pdf (complete markup), MAP_Novus_20250325.pdf (mutual action plan with milestones and signature deadlines)
